draft.title: Forming government
card: Australians vote for a member for each seat in the House of Representatives. There are 150 seats, so a majority is 76 seats.
The party, or the coalition of parties, that has a majority in the House of Representatives forms government. Its leader becomes Prime Minister.
Independents belong to no party. Sometimes no party or coalition wins 76 seats. This is called a hung parliament.

In a hung parliament, a party can form a minority government if enough independents or small parties promise to support it on votes about whether it can stay in power. It can then pass laws only with their help.
draft.remember: Government is formed by whoever can win the support of a majority in the House of Representatives.

a.q: After an election, the Orange Party holds 81 of the 150 seats in the House of Representatives. What happens?
opts: It forms government, as it has a majority of seats
It must ask independents to back it before it can govern
It forms a minority government with a hung parliament
It cannot govern until it wins a majority of the Senate
a.why: A majority in the House of Representatives is 76 seats or more, and 81 is above that. So the Orange Party forms government by itself. A hung parliament happens only when no party or coalition reaches 76.
a.clue: Compare 81 with the number needed for a majority.

b.q: At an election, the Blue Party wins 70 seats, the Green Alliance wins 68, and 12 seats go to independents and small parties. What is the most likely way a government is formed?
opts: A party wins the support of enough independents to govern
The party with the most seats governs without anyone's help
The two largest parties must form a coalition together
A new election is held straight away to choose a winner
b.why: No party has 76 seats, so this is a hung parliament. A party can form a minority government if enough independents back it. Having the most seats is not enough by itself, as 70 is short of a majority.
b.clue: Does 70 seats reach a majority of 150?

a.best: It forms government, as it has a majority of seats

b.best: A party wins the support of enough independents to govern

problems.detail: "It can then pass laws only with their help" is not accurate. A minority government can also pass a bill with the opposition's votes, and every bill must pass the Senate too. Better: "It usually needs their votes, or other members' votes, to pass laws in the House."

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear answer. The card's last line wrongly says a minority government can pass laws only with independents' help: the opposition could also vote for a bill, and the Senate must pass it too.
